title: tier-2 shipped code + state mode: orthonormalize a basis inside a preloaded snapshot
notes: STATE-MODE pilot. The basis pointee is a slice of a 0x200-byte snapshot at guest 0x200000000000+0x100; the whole snapshot is the state channel, compared after every call.
The candidate is the same shipped function as fn/OrthonormalizeCameraBasis-cargo; this unit proves the state preload/compare plumbing and the probe's guest-pointer translation.
The state region is declared by the `state` block, so reads inside it are not 'undeclared global reads'; all other image reads are listed in allowedImageReads.
Build binding: camera.rs + verify_probe.rs + git revision.

knownEquivalentMutants.rationale: The assert checks desc.len() >= 0x30. The state fixture always supplies 48 bytes at the guest slice, so lowering the bound to 0x2f cannot change any observable result for this unit; a 47-byte slice is outside the declared ptr_len.

The 0.008 unit-length boundary is a single f32 bit pattern. The fixture's nearest measures are 0.001999 and 0.0201; neither lands on it. Only an input with |len2-1| exactly 0.008 could observe the difference, and the oracle's own comiss/jae uses the same IEEE relation.

The |dot| > 0.004 gate is also a single f32 boundary. The fixture pins dot values just inside (0.003) and just outside (0.005); neither is exactly 0.004. Only an input whose |dot| is the exact f32 0.004 could observe the difference, and the oracle uses the same IEEE jae/jbe relation.
